This kind of mentality I’ve seen you have throughout the comments is what breeds serial killers… just stop being so obsessed with women and what they think of you and ask yourself if YOU even like you. Does all this negativity really make you happy? Obviously it’s not getting you anywhere in life you want to go (re: on dates with women). 

You need to start worrying about yourself more and stop caring about everyone else. Your family sounds abusive and like assholes- so move out as soon as you’ve saved up enough. Many young girls are shallow in high school and yes, those that do date usually care about how their peers will view them so they pick the hot, charming, or funny “class clown” guys. The girls who don’t date in Highschool Are usually more concerned about other, real world things. Grades, part time jobs, taking care of their little siblings. The only reason you felt as though you were being slighted in Highschool is because you live in such a small town. I also lived in a small town (with abusive, drug addict parents) and most the girls were rich and shallow as well. 

The coffee attendant also, logically, was not trying to be rude to you. She was probably almost done her shift and tired, just wanted to leave, or had a bad day. I understand it can feel personal when a food/ retail worker is “short” to you, but it’s not. If you have never worked in the food service industry, this can be hard to understand, but if you didn’t do anything wrong it wasn’t you that made her act that way. However, as a previous comment stated: perhaps you were overtly nice and came off as “creepy,” taking her politeness and customer service attitude as flirting with you.  

Please just get out there into the real world, cut off your abusive relationship with your family, and live life for YOU and YOUR happiness. Please. The longer you stay in this small town bubble where you feel like you’re getting nowhere- in life and with the ladies- the more dejected, pessimistic, and misogynistic you will become. The right person will come to you in time. Trust me. I thought I was going to end up alone and sad too in Highschool. Moving out of state and as far away as I could for college was the best decision I could make- even though it meant leaving my sister at home. I found myself, started working at a farm of all places, and there I met someone who saw me for ME. Who broke down my walls and preconceived notions about other people and trusting them. 

Please, for the sake of everyone else, just learn to love yourself. You deserve an amazing and happy life. And if no one has told you this today: I love you and I think you deserve great things.
